claim: Anillin is enriched in CNS myelin when biochemically purified from mouse brains at P75.
source: Indeed, anillin was detected in myelin when biochemically purified from mouse brains at P75, while it was virtually undetectable in brain lysates when loading the same amount of protein (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1A comparing myelin and brain lysate samples.

claim: Anillin is enriched in myelin similar to SEPT8 variant 1.
source: This implies that anillin is enriched in myelin similar to SEPT8 variant 1 (SEPT8_v1; according to nomenclature at Ensembl.org) (Patzig et al., 2016a) or myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) (Linnington et al., 1984).
evidence: Based on comparison with known myelin-enriched proteins and supported by citation to previous work on SEPT8_v1.

claim: Anillin-immunolabeling parallels but does not overlap with axonal neurofilament labeling.
source: We found that anillin-immunolabeling parallels but does not overlap with axonal neurofilament (NF) labeling (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry and confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Most anillin-immunolabeling is reminiscent of longitudinal myelin septin filaments.
source: Most anillin-immunolabeling was reminiscent of the longitudinal myelin septin filaments (Figure 1C) (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 1C and comparison with previous work on septin filaments.

claim: The abundance of ANLN in myelin increases with developmental maturation.
source: Indeed, by immunoblotting of myelin purified from mouse brains at postnatal day 15 (P15), P18, P21 and P24, the abundance of ANLN increased (Figure 1D) similar to that of SEPT2.
evidence: Supported by immunoblotting data across developmental timepoints shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Co-labeled structures of ANLN and SEPT8 were occasionally detected at P21 and frequently seen at P28 but not at P15.
source: When immunolabeling ANLN together with SEPT8 on longitudinal optic nerve sections at P15, P21 and P28, first co-labeled structures were occasionally detected at P21 but frequently seen at P28 (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data at different developmental timepoints shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Expression of the Anln gene is strongly enriched in mature oligodendrocytes.
source: In the adult CNS, expression of Anln mRNA is highest in myelinating oligodendrocytes when assessed by RNA-Seq (www.web.stanford.edu/group/barres_lab/cgi-bin/igv_cgi_2.py?lname=anln) (Zhang et al., 2014), single-cell transcriptomics (www.linnarssonlab.org/cortex) (Zeisel et al., 2015) and in situ-hybridization (mouse.brain-map.org/gene/show/44585) (Lein et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by multiple independent datasets including RNA-Seq, single-cell transcriptomics, and in situ hybridization.

claim: The abundance of Anln mRNA increases over 10-fold coinciding with the differentiation of oligodendrocyte progenitor cells to myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: Considering that the abundance of Anln mRNA increases over 10-fold coinciding with the differentiation of oligodendrocyte progenitor cells to myelinating oligodendrocytes (Zhang et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citation to published RNA-Seq data.

claim: Conditional mutants lacking ANLN in oligodendrocytes (Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice) were born at expected frequencies.
source: Conditional mutants and control mice were born at the expected frequencies, and the major white matter regions developed normally as judged by light microscopic visualization of myelin upon silver impregnation (Figure 2A,A').
evidence: Supported by observation of birth frequencies and silver impregnation data shown in Figure 2A,A'.

claim: Major white matter regions developed normally in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice as judged by light microscopic visualization of myelin upon silver impregnation.
source: Conditional mutants and control mice were born at the expected frequencies, and the major white matter regions developed normally as judged by light microscopic visualization of myelin upon silver impregnation (Figure 2A,A').
evidence: Supported by silver impregnation data shown in Figure 2A,A'.

claim: Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice exhibit numerous myelin outfoldings in the CNS.
source: However, electron microscopic analysis revealed the presence of numerous myelin outfoldings in the CNS of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice (Figure 2B,C), very similar to Sept8null/null and Sept8flox/flox;CnpCre/WT mutants (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2B,C and comparison with Sept8 mutants.

claim: Myelin outfoldings in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice are very similar to those in Sept8null/null and Sept8flox/flox;CnpCre/WT mutants.
source: However, electron microscopic analysis revealed the presence of numerous myelin outfoldings in the CNS of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice (Figure 2B,C), very similar to Sept8null/null and Sept8flox/flox;CnpCre/WT mutants (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy data and comparison with previously published Sept8 mutant phenotypes.

claim: Myelin sheath thickness is normal in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: Analysis of myelin sheath thickness (Figure 2D,D'), the percentage of myelinated axons (Figure 2E), degenerating/degenerated axons (Figure 2F) and secondary neuropathology (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) did not reveal further abnormalities in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice
evidence: Supported by g-ratio analysis shown in Figure 2D,D'.

claim: The percentage of myelinated axons is normal in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: Analysis of myelin sheath thickness (Figure 2D,D'), the percentage of myelinated axons (Figure 2E), degenerating/degenerated axons (Figure 2F) and secondary neuropathology (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) did not reveal further abnormalities in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The frequency of degenerating/degenerated axons is normal in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: Analysis of myelin sheath thickness (Figure 2D,D'), the percentage of myelinated axons (Figure 2E), degenerating/degenerated axons (Figure 2F) and secondary neuropathology (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) did not reveal further abnormalities in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Secondary neuropathology is not increased in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: Analysis of myelin sheath thickness (Figure 2D,D'), the percentage of myelinated axons (Figure 2E), degenerating/degenerated axons (Figure 2F) and secondary neuropathology (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) did not reveal further abnormalities in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Myelin outfoldings represent a very specific neuropathology in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: Analysis of myelin sheath thickness (Figure 2D,D'), the percentage of myelinated axons (Figure 2E), degenerating/degenerated axons (Figure 2F) and secondary neuropathology (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) did not reveal further abnormalities in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice, implying that myelin outfoldings represent a very specific neuropathology.
evidence: Inferred from the absence of other abnormalities in multiple analyses.

claim: Nerve conduction velocity is reduced by 15.5% in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice compared to control mice at 6 months of age.
source: Indeed, nerve conduction velocity was reduced by 15.5% in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT compared to control mice (Figure 2G), very similar to Sept8-mutants (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological measurements shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The reduction in nerve conduction velocity in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice is very similar to Sept8-mutants.
source: Indeed, nerve conduction velocity was reduced by 15.5% in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT compared to control mice (Figure 2G), very similar to Sept8-mutants (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by comparison with previously published data on Sept8 mutants.

claim: No nodal or paranodal abnormality was detected in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: This analysis did not reveal any nodal or paranodal abnormality in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C–F).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemical analysis of nodal and paranodal markers shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Myelin outfoldings are the most likely cause of reduced nerve conduction velocity in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: Although we cannot formally rule out other unidentified alterations in the CNS of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice, myelin outfoldings are the most likely cause of reduced nerve conduction velocity.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of myelin outfoldings and absence of other identified abnormalities.

claim: ANLN is undetectable by immunoblot analysis of myelin purified from the brains of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: As expected, ANLN was undetectable by immunoblot analysis of myelin purified from the brains of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The abundance of SEPT8 in myelin is reduced in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: Interestingly, in these mutants the abundance of SEPT8 in myelin was reduced (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ANLN was readily detectable in myelin purified from the brains of control mice but not identified in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT myelin by mass spectrometry.
source: ANLN was readily detectable in myelin purified from the brains of control mice but not identified in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT myelin (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by quantitative label-free mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The abundance of all myelin septins (SEPT2, SEPT4, SEPT7, SEPT8) is strongly reduced in myelin purified from the brains of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: The abundance of all myelin septins (SEPT2, SEPT4, SEPT7, SEPT8) was strongly reduced in myelin purified from the brains of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice (Figure 3A,B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by quantitative proteomics data shown in Figure 3A,B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The abundance of CDC42 and RHOB appears reduced in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT myelin, although less than the applied threshold of a 2-fold change.
source: Interestingly, the abundance of two GTPases of the Rho-subfamily, CDC42 and RHOB, also appeared reduced, although less than the applied threshold of a 2-fold change (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by quantitative proteomics data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The abundance of major myelin marker proteins is unaltered in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT myelin.
source: Importantly, the abundance of the major myelin marker proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3C) and cytoskeletal proteins associated with the actin cytoskeleton or microtubules (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D) was unaltered.
evidence: Supported by quantitative proteomics data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3C.

claim: The abundance of cytoskeletal proteins associated with the actin cytoskeleton or microtubules is unaltered in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT myelin.
source: Importantly, the abundance of the major myelin marker proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3C) and cytoskeletal proteins associated with the actin cytoskeleton or microtubules (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D) was unaltered.
evidence: Supported by quantitative proteomics data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: PtdIns(4,5)P2 abundance is decreased in myelin purified from the brains of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice compared to control mice.
source: Indeed, by quantitative assessment of label-free lipid extracts (Goebbels et al., 2010; König et al., 2008) we found a decreased abundance of PtdIns(4,5)P2 in myelin purified from the brains of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT compared to control mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by quantitative lipid analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: cDNA-fragments for Sept2, Sept4, Sept7, Sept8 were amplified with equal efficiency from mutant and control corpus callosi.
source: By qRT-PCR, cDNA-fragments for Sept2, Sept4, Sept7, Sept8 were amplified with equal efficiency from mutant and control corpus callosi (Figure 3E)
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The loss of myelin septins is a posttranscriptional event secondary to ANLN-deficiency.
source: By qRT-PCR, cDNA-fragments for Sept2, Sept4, Sept7, Sept8 were amplified with equal efficiency from mutant and control corpus callosi (Figure 3E), suggesting that the loss of myelin septins is a posttranscriptional event secondary to ANLN-deficiency.
evidence: Inferred from equal mRNA levels but reduced protein levels of septins.

claim: Myelin septin monomers are likely degraded if not incorporated into filamentous higher order structures, the formation of which is facilitated by ANLN.
source: Most likely, myelin septin monomers are degraded if not incorporated into filamentous higher order structures, the formation of which is facilitated by ANLN.
evidence: Speculative interpretation based on the observation of normal mRNA but reduced protein levels.

claim: cDNA fragments for Rhob and Cdc42 were amplified with equal efficiency from mutant and control corpus callosi.
source: The cDNA-fragments for Rhob and Cdc42 were also amplified with equal efficiency from mutant and control corpus callosi (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: cDNA fragments for Anln were virtually undetectable in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT corpus callosi.
source: Conversely, cDNA fragments for Anln were virtually undetectable in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT corpus callosi (Figure 3E)
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Expression of Anln mRNA in the adult CNS is strongly enriched in mature oligodendrocytes.
source: Conversely, cDNA fragments for Anln were virtually undetectable in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT corpus callosi (Figure 3E), indicating that expression of Anln mRNA in the adult CNS is strongly enriched in mature oligodendrocytes in accordance with RNA-Seq data (Zeisel et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: Inferred from the loss of Anln mRNA in oligodendrocyte-specific knockout and supported by published RNA-Seq data.

claim: Myelin outfoldings in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice measure between 10 µm and 15 µm in length.
source: The observed myelin outfoldings measured between 10 µm and 15 µm in length.
evidence: Based on FIB-SEM 3D reconstruction measurements.

claim: Myelin outfoldings represent large sheets of compacted multilayered membrane stacks that extend for considerable distance away from the myelinated axon.
source: Thus, myelin outfoldings do not adopt pin-needle-like shape but represent large sheets of compacted multilayered membrane stacks that extend for considerable distance away from the myelinated axon.
evidence: Based on FIB-SEM 3D reconstruction analysis.

claim: Most myelin outfoldings observed by FIB-SEM were in internodal segments.
source: Most of them were in internodal segments; we observed only a single myelin outfolding close to a node of Ranvier.
evidence: Based on FIB-SEM 3D reconstruction observations.

claim: Only a single myelin outfolding was observed close to a node of Ranvier by FIB-SEM.
source: Most of them were in internodal segments; we observed only a single myelin outfolding close to a node of Ranvier.
evidence: Based on FIB-SEM 3D reconstruction observations.

claim: Outfoldings of compact CNS myelin are a neuropathological hallmark in numerous models of myelin-related disorders.
source: Outfoldings of compact CNS myelin are a neuropathological hallmark in numerous models of myelin-related disorders (Patzig et al., 2016a) and upon normal brain aging (Peters, 2002; Sturrock, 1976).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature on myelin disorders and aging.

claim: Outfoldings of compact CNS myelin occur upon normal brain aging.
source: Outfoldings of compact CNS myelin are a neuropathological hallmark in numerous models of myelin-related disorders (Patzig et al., 2016a) and upon normal brain aging (Peters, 2002; Sturrock, 1976).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature on brain aging.

claim: Septin filaments are localized in the non-compacted adaxonal myelin layer underlying the innermost compact myelin membrane.
source: Localized in the non-compacted adaxonal myelin layer, i.e. underlying the innermost compact myelin membrane, septin filaments scaffold the myelin structure, thereby preventing the emergence of myelin outfoldings (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work on septin localization.

claim: Septin filaments scaffold the myelin structure, thereby preventing the emergence of myelin outfoldings.
source: Localized in the non-compacted adaxonal myelin layer, i.e. underlying the innermost compact myelin membrane, septin filaments scaffold the myelin structure, thereby preventing the emergence of myelin outfoldings (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work and the phenotype of septin mutants.

claim: The phenotype of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice is very similar to that of mice lacking SEPT8.
source: The phenotype of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice is very similar to that of mice lacking SEPT8, a septin monomer essential for the assembly of myelin septin filaments (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Based on comparison of myelin outfoldings and nerve conduction velocity between Anln and Sept8 mutants.

claim: SEPT8 is a septin monomer essential for the assembly of myelin septin filaments.
source: The phenotype of Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice is very similar to that of mice lacking SEPT8, a septin monomer essential for the assembly of myelin septin filaments (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work on SEPT8.

claim: Anillin is critical for the assembly of septin filaments in CNS myelin.
source: Thus, the present study has revealed that anillin is critical for the assembly of septin filaments in CNS myelin and that the lack of these filaments causes myelin outfoldings associated with reduced nerve conduction velocity.
evidence: Supported by the loss of septin filaments in Anln mutants and the resulting myelin outfoldings.

claim: The lack of septin filaments causes myelin outfoldings associated with reduced nerve conduction velocity.
source: Thus, the present study has revealed that anillin is critical for the assembly of septin filaments in CNS myelin and that the lack of these filaments causes myelin outfoldings associated with reduced nerve conduction velocity.
evidence: Supported by the phenotype of Anln mutants showing both myelin outfoldings and reduced nerve conduction velocity.

claim: During yeast cytokinesis, PtdIns(4,5)P2 recruits the anillin homolog Mid2p to the membrane at the cleavage furrow.
source: During yeast cytokinesis, PtdIns(4,5)P2 recruits the anillin homolog Mid2p to the membrane at the cleavage furrow, which in turn is critical for the polymerization of septin subunits into rings at the budding site of mother and daughter cells (Bertin et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on yeast cytokinesis.

claim: Mid2p is critical for the polymerization of septin subunits into rings at the budding site of mother and daughter cells in yeast.
source: During yeast cytokinesis, PtdIns(4,5)P2 recruits the anillin homolog Mid2p to the membrane at the cleavage furrow, which in turn is critical for the polymerization of septin subunits into rings at the budding site of mother and daughter cells (Bertin et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on yeast cytokinesis.

claim: The interactions between PtdIns(4,5)P2, anillin and septins are probably principally conserved between dividing cells and mature oligodendrocytes.
source: At the molecular level, the interactions between PtdIns(4,5)P2, anillin and septins are probably principally conserved between dividing cells and mature oligodendrocytes, which are post-mitotic.
evidence: Speculative inference based on similarities between yeast and oligodendrocyte systems.

claim: During cytokinesis, ANLN affects microtubules and myosin-dependent bundling of actin filaments.
source: Yet, during cytokinesis, ANLN affects microtubules and myosin-dependent bundling of actin filaments (Hickson and O'Farrell, 2008a; Hickson and O'Farrell, 2008b).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on cytokinesis.

claim: Myelin wrapping involves actin disassembly.
source: Since myelin wrapping involves actin disassembly (Nawaz et al., 2015; Zuchero et al., 2015) and myelin compaction requires trafficking of Mbp mRNA along microtubules (Müller et al., 2013; Thakurela et al., 2016)
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on myelin wrapping.

claim: Myelin compaction requires trafficking of Mbp mRNA along microtubules.
source: Since myelin wrapping involves actin disassembly (Nawaz et al., 2015; Zuchero et al., 2015) and myelin compaction requires trafficking of Mbp mRNA along microtubules (Müller et al., 2013; Thakurela et al., 2016)
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on myelin compaction.

claim: There is no evidence of fewer, thinner or non-compacted myelin sheaths in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
source: Since myelin wrapping involves actin disassembly (Nawaz et al., 2015; Zuchero et al., 2015) and myelin compaction requires trafficking of Mbp mRNA along microtubules (Müller et al., 2013; Thakurela et al., 2016), we point out that there is no evidence of fewer, thinner or non-compacted myelin sheaths in Anlnflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice.
evidence: Based on the absence of such phenotypes in the analyses performed.

claim: ANLN is required during the latest stages of myelin maturation for septin-dependent scaffolding of the myelin sheath.
source: Instead, ANLN is required during the latest stages of myelin maturation, i.e., for septin-dependent scaffolding of the myelin sheath rather than for its actin/tubulin-dependent biosynthesis and compaction.
evidence: Inferred from the timing of ANLN expression, the lack of early myelination defects, and the specific loss of septin filaments.

claim: ANLN is not required for actin/tubulin-dependent biosynthesis and compaction of myelin.
source: Instead, ANLN is required during the latest stages of myelin maturation, i.e., for septin-dependent scaffolding of the myelin sheath rather than for its actin/tubulin-dependent biosynthesis and compaction.
evidence: Inferred from the normal myelin formation and compaction in Anln mutants.

claim: Myelin is one of the most long-lived structures in the CNS.
source: Myelin is one of the most long-lived structures in the CNS (Toyama et al., 2013) with a particularly slow turnover rate of its components (Lasiene et al., 2009; Lüders et al., 2019; Yeung et al., 2014; Young et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on myelin longevity.

claim: Myelin has a particularly slow turnover rate of its components.
source: Myelin is one of the most long-lived structures in the CNS (Toyama et al., 2013) with a particularly slow turnover rate of its components (Lasiene et al., 2009; Lüders et al., 2019; Yeung et al., 2014; Young et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on myelin protein turnover.

claim: Failure to physically stabilize the myelin architecture causes myelin outfoldings and affects nerve conduction velocity.
source: Failure to physically stabilize the myelin architecture causes myelin outfoldings and affects nerve conduction velocity.
evidence: Inferred from the phenotype of Anln mutants lacking septin scaffolding.

claim: PtdIns(4,5)P2/anillin-dependent scaffolding of myelin by septin filaments represents a crucial step of myelin maturation.
source: We therefore propose that PtdIns(4,5)P2/anillin-dependent scaffolding of myelin by septin filaments represents a crucial step of myelin maturation.
evidence: Proposed based on the findings that loss of ANLN leads to loss of septins, myelin outfoldings, and reduced nerve conduction.

claim: Myelin serves as an axonal insulator that facilitates rapid nerve conduction along axons.
source: Myelin serves as an axonal insulator that facilitates rapid nerve conduction along axons.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about myelin function.

claim: A healthy myelin sheath comprises compacted membrane layers spiraling around the cross-sectioned axon by transmission electron microscopy.
source: By transmission electron microscopy, a healthy myelin sheath comprises compacted membrane layers spiraling around the cross-sectioned axon.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about myelin ultrastructure.

claim: The assembly of septin filaments in the innermost non-compacted myelin layer is one of the latest steps of myelin maturation in the CNS.
source: Previously we identified the assembly of septin filaments in the innermost non-compacted myelin layer as one of the latest steps of myelin maturation in the central nervous system (CNS) (Patzig et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Loss of anillin from oligodendrocytes disrupts myelin septin assembly.
source: Here we show that loss of the cytoskeletal adaptor protein anillin (ANLN) from oligodendrocytes disrupts myelin septin assembly, thereby causing the emergence of pathological myelin outfoldings.
evidence: Supported by the experimental findings in Anln mutant mice showing loss of septins.

claim: Loss of anillin from oligodendrocytes causes the emergence of pathological myelin outfoldings.
source: Here we show that loss of the cytoskeletal adaptor protein anillin (ANLN) from oligodendrocytes disrupts myelin septin assembly, thereby causing the emergence of pathological myelin outfoldings.
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy data showing myelin outfoldings in Anln mutants.

claim: Myelin outfoldings are a poorly understood hallmark of myelin disease and brain aging.
source: Since myelin outfoldings are a poorly understood hallmark of myelin disease and brain aging we assessed axon/myelin-units in Anln-mutant mice by focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM)
evidence: Supported by citations to literature on myelin disease and aging.

claim: Myelin outfoldings in Anln-mutant mice were three-dimensionally reconstructed as large sheets of multiple compact membrane layers by FIB-SEM.
source: Since myelin outfoldings are a poorly understood hallmark of myelin disease and brain aging we assessed axon/myelin-units in Anln-mutant mice by focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM); myelin outfoldings were three-dimensionally reconstructed as large sheets of multiple compact membrane layers.
evidence: Supported by FIB-SEM 3D reconstruction data.

claim: Anillin-dependent assembly of septin filaments scaffolds mature myelin sheaths, facilitating rapid nerve conduction in the healthy CNS.
source: We suggest that anillin-dependent assembly of septin filaments scaffolds mature myelin sheaths, facilitating rapid nerve conduction in the healthy CNS.
evidence: Proposed based on the findings that loss of anillin leads to loss of septin scaffolding, myelin outfoldings, and reduced nerve conduction.

claim: Fast, saltatory nerve impulse conduction in the CNS of vertebrates is facilitated by the ensheathment of axons with multiple layers of insulating oligodendroglial membrane, termed myelin.
source: Fast, saltatory nerve impulse conduction in the central nervous system (CNS) of vertebrates is facilitated by the ensheathment of axons with multiple layers of insulating oligodendroglial membrane, termed myelin (Nave and Werner, 2014; Hartline and Colman, 2007).
evidence: Established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Myelin compaction along the extracellular membrane surface involves cholesterol-associated transmembrane proteins, such as proteolipid protein (PLP).
source: Myelin compaction along the extracellular membrane surface (intraperiod line) involves cholesterol-associated transmembrane proteins, such as proteolipid protein (PLP) (Simons et al., 2000; Werner et al., 2013)
evidence: Established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: PLP exhibits adhesive forces that prevent splitting of myelin lamellae.
source: Myelin compaction along the extracellular membrane surface (intraperiod line) involves cholesterol-associated transmembrane proteins, such as proteolipid protein (PLP) (Simons et al., 2000; Werner et al., 2013), which exhibits adhesive forces (Bakhti et al., 2013; Bizzozero et al., 2001) that prevent splitting of myelin lamellae (Lüders et al., 2017; Möbius et al., 2016; Rosenbluth et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on PLP function.

claim: At the intracellular membrane surface (major dense line), myelin basic protein (MBP) facilitates the tight association of myelin layers by covering the negatively charged headgroups of membrane phospholipids.
source: At the intracellular membrane surface (major dense line), myelin basic protein (MBP) facilitates the tight association of myelin layers by covering the negatively charged headgroups of membrane phospholipids (Musse et al., 2008; Nawaz et al., 2009; Nawaz et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on MBP function.

claim: The adhesive function of MBP can be counteracted by the presence of cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase (CNP).
source: The adhesive function of MBP can be counteracted by the presence of cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase (CNP), thereby regulating the developmental closure of cytoplasmic channels that flank compacted myelin (Snaidero et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work on CNP function.

claim: CNP regulates the developmental closure of cytoplasmic channels that flank compacted myelin.
source: The adhesive function of MBP can be counteracted by the presence of cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase (CNP), thereby regulating the developmental closure of cytoplasmic channels that flank compacted myelin (Snaidero et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work on CNP function.

claim: In mature myelin, CNP is largely confined to non-compacted myelin.
source: In mature myelin, CNP is thus largely confined to non-compacted myelin (Brunner et al., 1989; Trapp et al., 1988).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on CNP localization.

claim: The relevance of PLP, MBP and CNP for the regular ultrastructure of myelin is reflected by their high abundance in biochemically purified myelin membranes.
source: The relevance of PLP, MBP and CNP for the regular ultrastructure of myelin is reflected by their high abundance in biochemically purified myelin membranes (Jahn et al., 2009) and the myelin defects in the corresponding mouse mutants.
evidence: Supported by citation to proteomics data and knowledge of mutant phenotypes.

claim: Myelin defects occur in mouse mutants lacking PLP, MBP, or CNP.
source: The relevance of PLP, MBP and CNP for the regular ultrastructure of myelin is reflected by their high abundance in biochemically purified myelin membranes (Jahn et al., 2009) and the myelin defects in the corresponding mouse mutants.
evidence: Implied by the statement about myelin defects in corresponding mouse mutants.

claim: Pathological destabilization of myelin was observed as pathological outfoldings of entire stacks of compacted myelin membranes in several myelin mutants.
source: In addition to the delamination of single myelin layers, pathological destabilization of myelin was observed as pathological outfoldings of entire stacks of compacted myelin membranes in several myelin mutants, (Patzig et al., 2016a) and upon normal brain aging (Peters, 2002; Sturrock, 1976).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on myelin mutants and aging.

claim: Myelin outfoldings correlate with a loss of septins.
source: We recently found that myelin outfoldings correlate with a loss of septins, which are cytoskeletal proteins of comparatively lower abundance in the myelin proteome (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Septins are cytoskeletal proteins of comparatively lower abundance in the myelin proteome.
source: We recently found that myelin outfoldings correlate with a loss of septins, which are cytoskeletal proteins of comparatively lower abundance in the myelin proteome (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous proteomics work.

claim: Septins are widely expressed and control the rigidity of the membranes they are associated with.
source: Septins are widely expressed and control the rigidity of the membranes they are associated with (Bridges and Gladfelter, 2015; Gilden and Krummel, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on septin function.

claim: Myelin septin filaments are localized in the non-compacted, adaxonal myelin layer adjacent to the inner-most compacted myelin membrane.
source: Localized in the non-compacted, adaxonal myelin layer adjacent to the inner-most compacted myelin membrane, myelin septin filaments are assembled from the monomers SEPT2, SEPT4, SEPT7 and SEPT8 in 1:1:2:2 stoichiometry (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work on septin localization.

claim: Myelin septin filaments are assembled from the monomers SEPT2, SEPT4, SEPT7 and SEPT8 in 1:1:2:2 stoichiometry.
source: Localized in the non-compacted, adaxonal myelin layer adjacent to the inner-most compacted myelin membrane, myelin septin filaments are assembled from the monomers SEPT2, SEPT4, SEPT7 and SEPT8 in 1:1:2:2 stoichiometry (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work on septin composition.

claim: The composition of myelin septin filaments marks a canonical but distinct composition of subunits when compared with the higher order structures of septins in other cell types.
source: This marks a canonical but distinct composition of subunits when compared with the higher order structures of septins in other cell types (Barral and Kinoshita, 2008; Dolat et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on septin structures in other cell types.

claim: Septin filaments provide a scaffold that prevents detachment of the compacted myelin layers from the adaxonal myelin membrane and thus outfoldings of entire myelin sheaths.
source: Recently, we proposed that septin filaments provide a scaffold that prevents detachment of the compacted myelin layers from the adaxonal myelin membrane and thus outfoldings of entire myelin sheaths (Patzig et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work proposing this model.

claim: Septins associate with the pleckstrin homology (PH)-domain containing adaptor protein anillin (ANLN) and its homologs in drosophila embryos.
source: Septins associate with the pleckstrin homology (PH)-domain containing adaptor protein anillin (ANLN) and its homologs in drosophila embryos (El Amine et al., 2013; Field et al., 2005; Liu et al., 2012)

claim: Septins associate with anillin homologs in budding yeast.

evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on septin-anillin interactions in yeast.

claim: Septins associate with anillin in mouse NIH3T3-fibroblasts.

claim: The role of anillin in the formation of contractile septin rings is a conserved step of cytokinesis.
source: Here, the role of anillin in the formation of contractile septin rings is a conserved step of cytokinesis (Piekny and Maddox, 2010) and essential for cell division (Zhang and Maddox, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work on anillin in cytokinesis.

claim: Anillin is essential for cell division.

claim: Oligodendroglial anillin serves a crucial function in myelination.
source: Here we show that oligodendroglial anillin serves a crucial function in myelination.
evidence: Supported by the experimental findings showing myelin defects in Anln mutants.

claim: This work establishes a crucial function for anillin-dependent assembly of myelin septin filaments in scaffolding CNS myelin to enable rapid nerve conduction.
source: This work thus establishes a crucial function for anillin-dependent assembly of myelin septin filaments in scaffolding CNS myelin to enable rapid nerve conduction, thereby demonstrating a vital function of anillin unrelated to cytokinesis.
evidence: Supported by the experimental findings showing loss of septins, myelin outfoldings, and reduced nerve conduction in Anln mutants.

claim: This work demonstrates a vital function of anillin unrelated to cytokinesis.
source: This work thus establishes a crucial function for anillin-dependent assembly of myelin septin filaments in scaffolding CNS myelin to enable rapid nerve conduction, thereby demonstrating a vital function of anillin unrelated to cytokinesis.
evidence: Inferred from the function of anillin in post-mitotic oligodendrocytes.

claim: A reduction of PtdIns(4,5)P2 in myelin of Ptenflox/flox;CnpCre/WT mice causes a loss of septins and ANLN.

evidence: Supported by citation to previous work on Pten mutants.
